ordinance: Zoning Ordinance No. 192 of 1958, as amended through December 1967
map_title: City of Pittsburgh Zoning Map dated December 28, 1967, digitized by Details Reviewed (Western Pennsylvania Regional Data Center, CC BY)
structure: Section 301 divides the city into five types of district (S, R, I, C, M) and twenty classifications, each with its own article. Each article gives permitted uses, height and area rules, and use exceptions granted by Council, the Board of Adjustment or the Administrator.
hierarchy: Not cumulative: each district permits only the uses listed in its own article and its exceptions, so uses do not carry up automatically. Section 301 says a lower numbered district is more protected within its type, and each of the five types is most protected within itself.
boundary_rule: Section 302: boundaries follow the heavy solid map lines. A boundary in a street or way runs at its center, and stays if the street is vacated. Off-street boundaries follow a recorded lot line where the map indicates one, otherwise map scale.
method: Boundaries are the published digitization, clipped to land, and were not read from a scan for this atlas. Rules for the districts added after 1958 come from the ordinance text with its amendments. Districts carried over keep their 1958 limits; later amendments changed some of their details, such as exceptions and how height is measured, and these are not all shown. Each of today's tax parcels (Allegheny County, October 2026) takes the district covering most of it, and parcels are merged by census block for this map. Today's lots are not the lots of 1967.

form_notes.lot_sqft_per_unit: For multiple dwellings, the figure for a two-bedroom unit; two-family houses in R2. The S district requires this lot size only for a house, which needs the Administrator's approval.
